title: Ginzburg-Landau Theory for Confined Thin-Film Superconductors
summary: We develop a Ginzburg-Landau theory for superconducting thin films under quantum confinement. Starting from the Ginzburg-Landau theory and the recently developed confinement theory of metallic thin films, explicit analytical expressions are derived for the coherence length, penetration depth, electronic mean free path, and Ginzburg-Landau parameter in confined geometries. The central result is that quantum confinement directly renormalizes the intrinsic superconducting coherence length through confinement-induced modifications of the electronic density of states and Fermi energy.
